# Hello Clause

A reusable connected clause whose `say` action replaces text at a configured document location and emits `Hello Said`. Named connections determine how the action is invoked; the type declares no automatic invocation.

## Text and action behavior

`bindings.text` is required and has no default path. It must be a text pointer beginning with `/`, other than `/` itself, identifying the destination in the document where the clause executes. It is a destination path, not the greeting itself.

The action parameter `text` defaults to `"Hello World"`. Connection `params` override action defaults. This is an invocation default, not an initial value for the bound document location; an absent stored value remains unknown.

When execution reaches `say`, it rejects a non-text `text` with `Hello text must be Text`. Otherwise it appends a `replace` change at `bindings.text` and emits `Hello Said` with:

- `clause`: the clause instance key.
- `connection`: the invoking connection name.
- `text`: the text used for the replacement.

An invocation attempt does not establish that these effects committed. `Hello Said` describes the document action, not external delivery or audible speech.

## Connections and guards

`bindings.say` is a dictionary of named connection objects. Each connection requires an `on` mode and may specify `params`, `when`, `before`, `after`, and `once`.

- `params` supplies action arguments. Source data is available as `trigger`, rather than automatically becoming `text`: this is the workflow request, the inner embedded event, the timer’s stored arming trigger, or the source event for other modes.
- `when` defaults to `true`; a false condition skips execution without running the action.
- `parameters.conditions.say` supplies an additional action condition, defaulting to `true`. Failure rejects execution with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`. Conditions naming other actions are rejected.
- `before` runs after the conditions pass and before the action body; `after` runs after the body.
- `once` must be Boolean and defaults to `false`. When enabled, execution that reaches the end of `after` marks that connection as fired, and later invocations are skipped. This restriction applies separately to each connection.

Supported `on` modes are:

- `event`: a triggered-event source, optionally filtered by `event`.
- `channel`: an existing named `channel`, optionally filtered by `event`.
- `change`: updates at a required non-root `path`, optionally filtered by `event`.
- `embedded` and `collection`: embedded events at `path`, or from descendants beneath the collection `path`. Both require a non-root pointer and accept an `event` filter. Boolean `embed` defaults to enabled; `false` omits the automatic embedding contribution.
- `initialized`: `Clauses Initialized`, representing successful initial clause installation.
- `activated`: `Document Activated`.
- `workflow`: an operation using an authenticated channel selected by `party`, falling back to `channel`. It can carry a `request` declaration and an `event` filter. The configured channel governs invocation; the existence of this action grants no viewer permission.
- `timer`: invocation from an admitted timer firing, configured as below.

Clause and connection names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, or `~`. Unknown property/action bindings and unsupported connection fields are rejected.

## Timer connections

A timer requires exactly one of `timestamp` and `afterEvent`:

- `timestamp` is an integer Unix timestamp in microseconds, from `0` through `9007199254740991`. Scheduling is requested on initialization. Absolute timers reject `delayMs` and `policy`.
- `afterEvent` selects an event, channel, change, embedded, or collection source. It requires integer `delayMs` from `1` through `9007199254740`, measured from the source’s bound timestamp, not a clock read. A deadline exceeding `9007199254740991` is rejected. `policy` defaults to `first`, which suppresses further arming once armed; `latest` permits subsequent scheduling requests. Initialization cannot be the relative arming source.

Optional `cancelOn` must name a nonempty source and emits a cancellation request for the connection’s keyed timer. It supports the relative arming source kinds and initialization. Scheduling and cancellation requests do not themselves confirm a firing or cancellation outcome.

## Connection state and configuration

Each connection has state at `/connectionState_<clauseKey>/say.<connectionName>` in the executing document. Planned initial values are `armed: false` and `fired: false`. Timer arming sets `armed` to `true`; the supplied logic does not clear it on firing or cancellation, so it does not mean a timer is currently pending. `fired` is set only by completed execution with `once: true`; it is not a general execution history. A missing state value is unknown, not an inferred initial value.

The inherited transition rule rejects changing an existing clause configuration under the same clause key with `CONNECTIONS_REQUIRE_NEW_CLAUSE_KEY`; a changed configuration requires a new key.
